basic_information.name: Dify
basic_information.creator: LangGenius Inc. (founded by Luyu Zhang and John Wang in 2023; registered in Middletown, United States with engineering team in China)
basic_information.description: Dify is an open-source LLM application development platform that combines Backend-as-a-Service with LLMOps to let users visually build production-grade AI applications through drag-and-drop agentic workflows, RAG knowledge pipelines, agent orchestration, and model management. With 100k+ GitHub stars and a plugin marketplace, Dify stands out as the most popular open-source low-code AI platform, enabling entrepreneurs to go from idea to deployed AI app (chatbot, workflow, agent) without deep engineering expertise. Its self-hosting option with Docker makes it particularly attractive for teams needing data sovereignty and cost control compared to fully proprietary alternatives.
basic_information.release_date: 2023 (initial open-source release; v1.0.0 with plugin ecosystem launched February 2025; v1.6.0 with MCP support in 2025)

technical_capabilities.underlying_models: Multi-provider: supports hundreds of proprietary and open-source LLMs from dozens of inference providers. Proprietary: OpenAI (GPT-4o, GPT-4, GPT-3.5), Anthropic (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Opus), Google (Gemini), Azure OpenAI, Mistral AI. Open-source: Llama 3, Qwen, ChatGLM, DeepSeek, and any model available on Replicate or Hugging Face. Local deployment via Ollama, LocalAI, or Xinference. Supports any OpenAI API-compatible model endpoint.
technical_capabilities.customization_depth: workflow-builder | code-extension. Dify provides a visual drag-and-drop workflow builder for creating complex AI pipelines, plus code blocks (Python, JavaScript) within workflows for custom logic. Users can define custom tools, extend via the plugin system, and customize RAG pipeline components (chunking, embedding, retrieval). The plugin architecture (v1.0+) allows deep extension of models, tools, and agent strategies.
technical_capabilities.api_access: Yes. Full RESTful API for all application types. Every Dify app automatically gets a corresponding API endpoint. SDK support available. APIs allow separating prompts from business logic while utilizing the management interface for monitoring.
technical_capabilities.deployment_options: Cloud-hosted (dify.ai SaaS), self-hosted via Docker Compose (primary self-host method), embeddable web chat widget (JavaScript snippet, iframe, floating button), standalone WebApp portal, API-driven integration, AWS Marketplace (Dify Premium), Azure Marketplace (Dify Enterprise), managed hosting via Elestio and other providers.
technical_capabilities.ai_model_flexibility: multi-provider | bring-your-own-model. Users can freely switch between any supported model provider by entering API keys. Local models supported via Ollama, LocalAI, Xinference. Different workflow nodes can use different models. The plugin system allows adding new model providers. No vendor lock-in whatsoever.

user_experience.target_user: developer | business_user | enterprise_team. Dify targets both non-technical users who want to build AI apps through visual workflows and developers who want to accelerate production AI application development. Product design is aimed at ordinary users while also catering to developers through code extensions and APIs.
user_experience.learning_curve: hours. Basic chatbot or knowledge base app creation is achievable in under an hour with the visual builder and templates. Complex multi-step agentic workflows with custom tools take days to master. The Dify Workshop tutorial series is designed for complete beginners.
user_experience.setup_time: 10-15 minutes for cloud version (signup, add API key, create first app from template). 30-60 minutes for self-hosted Docker Compose deployment.
user_experience.collaboration_features: Multi-user workspaces as the basic unit of team collaboration. Role-based access control (RBAC) with four distinct roles. Members can create and edit applications and knowledge bases within shared workspaces. Workflow DSL export/import for sharing between teams. Enterprise Edition extends with multi-workspace setups, SSO, and audit logs.
user_experience.template_library: Built-in template library accessible from Studio > Create from Template. High-quality application templates created by Dify's prompt engineering team covering common scenarios: Knowledge Retrieval + Chatbot, Three-Step Translation Workflow, DeepResearch automation, and more. Additionally, the Dify Marketplace hosts 120+ plugins including models, tools, agent strategies, extensions, and bundles. Open-source frontend WebApp templates (MIT licensed) are available for custom development.
user_experience.visual_builder_type: drag-drop | hybrid. Canvas-based visual workflow builder where users connect nodes (LLM, knowledge retrieval, code, conditional logic, HTTP requests, tools) to create complex AI pipelines. The workflow engine uses a queued graph execution model supporting complex parallel scenarios and flexible node wiring. Also supports form-based app creation for simpler chatbot configurations.

ai_and_rag_capabilities.rag_support: Comprehensive built-in RAG pipeline called Knowledge Pipeline. Visual pipeline for transforming enterprise data into high-quality LLM context. Supports document upload (PDF, PPT, DOCX, TXT, and other common formats), URL ingestion, and custom data sources. Pluggable components for uploading, parsing, chunking, and embedding. Hybrid retrieval with configurable top-k and optional reranking. Integrations with vector stores including Milvus/Zilliz, TiDB, Weaviate, Qdrant, and pgvector. Multimodal Knowledge Base unifying text and images for vision-enabled RAG. Agentic RAG support where agents iteratively analyze intent, select tools, rewrite queries, and evaluate evidence.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.agent_capabilities: multi-step | multi-agent | autonomous. Agent Node enables agentic workflows with autonomous reasoning. Supports both LLM Function Calling and ReAct agent strategies. 50+ built-in tools (Google Search, DALL-E, Stable Diffusion, WolframAlpha, and more). Custom tool creation supported. Agents can iteratively analyze intent, select tools and sources, rewrite queries, evaluate evidence, and retry or fall back. The plugin system allows adding custom agent strategies.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.model_selection: Multi-vendor and BYOM (bring your own model). Users can freely switch between dozens of model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Azure, Hugging Face, Replicate, and more). Different nodes in the same workflow can use different models. Self-hosted local models supported via Ollama, LocalAI, Xinference. New model providers can be added via the plugin system.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.prompt_management: Built-in prompt configuration with system prompts, temperature and parameter controls, and response formatting per LLM node. LLMOps capabilities for monitoring and analyzing application logs and performance over time. Continuous improvement of prompts, datasets, and models based on production data. Annotation and fine-tuning support for iterative prompt optimization.

integration_and_ecosystem.key_integrations: Slack (via plugin), Discord, GitHub, Google Search, DALL-E, Stable Diffusion, WolframAlpha, Perplexity, Tavily (live web data), custom REST APIs via HTTP Request nodes, webhooks for external triggers. Database integrations through vector stores (Milvus, TiDB, Weaviate, Qdrant, pgvector). AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, Langfuse (observability), and custom tool plugins.
integration_and_ecosystem.integration_count: 120+ plugins in the Dify Marketplace (as of v1.0.0, February 2025), covering models, tools, agent strategies, extensions, and bundles. 50+ built-in tools for AI agents. Growing ecosystem with community-contributed plugins.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_support: Yes. Full two-way MCP (Model Context Protocol) support since v1.6.0. Supports HTTP-based MCP services (protocol 2025-03-26) with pre-authorized and auth-free modes. Dify workflows and agents can be turned into a standard MCP server, making them accessible across unlimited MCP clients. Also functions as an MCP client consuming external MCP services.
integration_and_ecosystem.webhook_support: Yes. Webhook and API trigger support for custom automations. HTTP Request nodes in workflows allow outbound webhooks. Inbound triggers via API endpoints. The Trigger system enables event-driven workflow execution from external sources.
integration_and_ecosystem.export_formats: Embeddable web chat widget (JavaScript snippet, iframe, floating button), standalone WebApp portal, RESTful API endpoint, workflow DSL export files (JSON-based, for sharing and importing between instances), open-source frontend WebApp templates (MIT license, React/Next.js) for custom development and rebranding. Docker-based self-hosted deployment.

pricing_and_accessibility.pricing_model: open-source | freemium | subscription | usage-based. Core platform is open-source and free to self-host. Cloud version offers freemium model with subscription tiers plus usage-based message credits.
pricing_and_accessibility.free_tier_limits: Sandbox (free): 200 messages (API calls), 1 user, 5 apps, 50MB knowledge storage. No credit card required. Self-hosted community edition is completely free with no usage limits (bring your own model API keys and infrastructure).
pricing_and_accessibility.paid_plans: Professional: $59/workspace/month - 3 team members, 50 apps, 5,000 message credits/month, enhanced limits. Team: $159/workspace/month - 50 team members, 200 apps, 10,000 message credits/month, 1,000 knowledge documents, 20GB storage. Enterprise: custom pricing - unlimited team members, SSO, audit logs, multi-workspace, dedicated support, private deployment. Dify Premium on AWS Marketplace with custom branding option. Free for students and educators.
pricing_and_accessibility.open_source: Yes (Dify Open Source License, based on Apache 2.0 with additional conditions). Core platform is fully open-source. Additional conditions: cannot use source code to operate a multi-tenant SaaS service competing with Dify without written authorization; cannot remove Dify logo or copyright information from the console. Plugins and WebApp templates are MIT licensed.
pricing_and_accessibility.self_hosting_option: Yes, straightforward. Primary method is Docker Compose: clone the repository, run docker compose commands. All state stored in PostgreSQL (metadata) and filesystem (data), making instances stateless and easily rebuildable. Also supports source code deployment for advanced customization. Comprehensive documentation available. Managed hosting via Elestio, Pigsty, and others.
pricing_and_accessibility.data_residency_and_sovereignty: Self-hosted deployment gives full control over data location and processing, enabling GDPR compliance by design. All data stays on your own infrastructure when self-hosted. Cloud version processes data on Dify's servers (location not explicitly specified as EU). Managed hosting providers like Elestio offer ISO 27001, SOC2, and GDPR-compliant EU hosting. Self-hosted + local models (via Ollama/DeepSeek) enables fully air-gapped private AI deployment with zero data leaving the organization. No explicit EU AI Act readiness certification as of early 2026.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in the open-source low-code/no-code AI application platform category. Dify has the largest reputation and most GitHub stars compared to similar open-source products (Flowise, Langflow, etc.), making it the de facto standard for open-source LLM app development. Positioned between simple chatbot builders and developer-centric frameworks, it serves as the go-to platform for teams wanting production-grade AI apps without starting from scratch.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: 130,000+ AI applications created on the cloud service. Used across industries from biomedicine to automotive. Recognized as AWS Social Impact Partner of the Year. Available on Microsoft Azure Marketplace and AWS Marketplace. Over 180,000 developers on the platform. Specific enterprise customer names not publicly disclosed, but enterprise customers span organizations across various industries.
adoption_and_market.community_size: 100,000+ GitHub stars (top 100 open-source projects globally). 290+ community contributors. 180,000+ registered developers. 59,000+ end users. 130,000+ AI applications created. Active community on GitHub Discussions, Discord, and the Dify Marketplace.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total funding: $11.5M. Investors include 5Y Capital, Alibaba Cloud Computing, FutureX Capital, Beijing Delian Yuntong Investment Management, and China Growth Capital. Seed round completed. Selected for TechCrunch Startup Battlefield 200 (September 2024). Revenue: $3.1M as of June 2025. Team size: 28-60 employees (sources vary). Founded 2023, rapid growth trajectory.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main competitors: Flowise (Apache 2.0, focused on rapid chatbot development, simpler but less comprehensive), Langflow (MIT, specialized in RAG pipelines, LangChain-native), n8n (fair-code, workflow automation focus, 12k records/min processing), Botpress (open-source conversational AI, more developer-centric). Also competes with proprietary platforms: Voiceflow (no-code chatbots), Stack AI (enterprise), and custom LangChain/LlamaIndex development. Dify differentiates through: (1) largest open-source community and ecosystem, (2) comprehensive all-in-one platform (workflows + RAG + agents + LLMOps), (3) easy self-hosting, (4) model-agnostic multi-provider support, (5) production-ready with enterprise features.
adoption_and_market.ecosystem_lock_in_risk: low. Fully open-source core with self-hosting option eliminates vendor dependency. Workflows exportable as DSL files. Standard API interfaces. Multi-provider model support prevents model lock-in. The main lock-in factor is the visual workflow format (DSL), but since the platform is open-source, organizations retain full control of their data and logic. Can be forked and customized if needed.

teaching_and_classroom.class_project_idea:
Project 1: 'Startup Knowledge Base Chatbot' (60 min) - Students sign up for the free Sandbox plan on dify.ai, create a new Chatflow app from the Knowledge Retrieval + Chatbot template, upload 3-5 pages of documentation about a fictional startup (product FAQ, pricing page, support articles), configure the LLM node with a custom system prompt defining the chatbot's persona (e.g., friendly startup support agent), test conversations with the knowledge base, and publish as a shareable WebApp link. Deliverable: working chatbot URL + 2-slide pitch analyzing how this reduces customer support costs and what the unit economics look like (cost per conversation vs. human support agent).

Project 2: 'AI-Powered Business Process Workflow' (75 min) - Students use the visual workflow builder to create a multi-step AI automation: an incoming customer inquiry is classified by intent (support vs. sales vs. feedback) using an LLM node, routed through conditional branches, processed with different prompts per category, and outputs a structured response plus a summary for the team. Students configure the LLM node, add conditional logic, use HTTP Request nodes to simulate CRM integration, and test the complete pipeline. Deliverable: working workflow demo + analysis of which business processes in their startup idea could be automated with similar AI workflows, with estimated time/cost savings.

teaching_and_classroom.student_prerequisites: basic prompting. Students should understand basic prompting concepts (how to write clear instructions for an AI model). No coding required for core features. The visual builder and template library make it accessible to complete beginners. Understanding of what an API is helps but is not mandatory.
teaching_and_classroom.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt Engineering & No-Code Tools) - primary fit. Students build a working AI chatbot with RAG knowledge base using the visual builder, applying prompt engineering in practice. Also relevant to Session 3 (Framing & Managing AI Projects) for Build vs Buy analysis (Dify self-hosted vs. proprietary SaaS vs. custom development), and Session 5 (Ethics & Governance) for discussing data sovereignty and self-hosting as a GDPR compliance strategy.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Dify is ideal for early-stage startups (pre-seed to Series A) with 1-15 person teams who want to build AI-powered products without a dedicated ML engineering team. Best suited for: (1) Customer-facing AI products - chatbots, knowledge assistants, AI-powered support that can be deployed as WebApps or embedded widgets in days; (2) Internal AI tools - document Q&A systems, automated workflows, data analysis pipelines for operational efficiency; (3) AI-first MVPs - startups whose core product is an AI application can use Dify as their backend, getting RAG, agent orchestration, and multi-model support out of the box. The self-hosted option is a major differentiator: startups in regulated industries (healthcare, finance, legal) or EU-based companies needing GDPR compliance can deploy Dify on their own infrastructure with local models, achieving full data sovereignty at minimal cost. The free self-hosted edition removes the cost barrier entirely for bootstrapped startups.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_mvp: Hours to days. A basic knowledge base chatbot MVP can be built and deployed in 2-4 hours using the cloud version with templates. A more complex multi-step agentic workflow with custom tools takes 2-5 days. Self-hosted deployment adds 1-2 hours for Docker setup. Compared to building from scratch with LangChain/LlamaIndex (weeks to months), Dify compresses the timeline by 10-50x for standard AI application patterns.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Dify when: you need a production-ready AI application platform quickly, your team lacks deep ML/NLP engineering expertise, you want model flexibility without vendor lock-in, you need self-hosting for data sovereignty, or you want visual workflow building for rapid iteration. Build custom when: you have unique performance requirements that need low-level optimization, your use case doesn't fit the workflow paradigm, or you need specialized ML pipelines beyond LLM orchestration. Choose proprietary alternatives (Voiceflow, Stack AI) when: you need polished no-code UX for non-technical teams, dedicated support/SLA, or specific channel integrations. Cost comparison: Dify self-hosted is free (infrastructure costs only, ~$20-100/month on a VPS); Dify Cloud Professional at $59/month is competitive with alternatives; at scale, self-hosting becomes dramatically cheaper than any SaaS alternative.
key_lessons: 1. Self-hosting is your strategic advantage: Unlike proprietary platforms, Dify's open-source nature means you own your AI infrastructure. Self-host from day one to maintain data sovereignty, avoid vendor lock-in, and dramatically reduce costs as you scale. A $50/month server can handle what would cost $500+/month on proprietary platforms.

2. Start with RAG, graduate to agents: The fastest path to value is uploading your existing content (docs, FAQs, product pages) as a knowledge base and deploying a RAG-powered chatbot. Once this is working and providing value, layer on agentic workflows for more complex automation. Don't over-engineer from the start.

3. Model flexibility is a business moat: Dify's multi-provider support means you're never locked into one AI vendor. Start with OpenAI for quality, experiment with Mistral or DeepSeek for cost optimization, and use local models via Ollama for sensitive data. This flexibility lets you optimize cost/quality tradeoffs as your business evolves.

4. The visual workflow is your documentation: Dify's drag-and-drop workflows serve double duty as both implementation and documentation of your AI logic. This makes it easy to onboard new team members, audit AI behavior, and iterate on business processes without losing institutional knowledge in code.

5. Plan for the plugin ecosystem: With 120+ plugins and growing, Dify's marketplace can extend your AI applications rapidly. Before building custom integrations, check if a plugin already exists. Contributing plugins back to the ecosystem also builds community credibility for your startup.
